newsitem.title: USA: U.S. adds Cali cartel "fronts" to banned list.
newsitem.headline: U.S. adds Cali cartel "fronts" to banned list.

text.p: The United States on Wednesday ordered economic sanctions against 78 businesses and individuals it said were "fronts" for the Cali drug cartel in Colombia, the White House announced.

The names were added to the administration's list of Specially Designated Narcotics Traffickers (SDNTs), making it illegal for Americans to do business with them and freezing any of their assets found within U.S. jurisdiction.

"The Treasury Department added to its list of SDNTs the names of 78 businesses and individuals that it has determined are acting as fronts for the Cali cartel -- the largest drug ring in the world and responsible for more than 80 percent of the cocaine that enters the United States," White House press secretary Mike McCurry said in a written statement.
"The Treasury action will have a chilling effect on cartel activity by further exposing, isolating, and incapacitating its agents," he added.
All 78 -- 21 businesses and 57 individuals -- of the new SDNTs had been determined to be owned or controlled by, or to act for or on behalf of the Cali cartel's "Pacho" Herrera Buitrago organisation.
Their addition to the list brings the total number of SDNTs to 359, since President Bill Clinton's Oct. 1995 executive order applying economic sanctions against Colombian drug cartels.
Violations of the restrictions carry criminal penalties of up to 10 years in prison and fines of $500,000 for corporations and $250,000 for individuals.
The White House said all of the listed SDNTs had been determined to be directly involved with illegal traffickers and their "so-called legitimate business empires."

"Such businesses include several large poultry farms and processing plants, investment and import/export firms, real estate developers, a consulting firm, a lumber distributor and a construction company," it said in a fact sheet accompanying the announcement.

"The Treasury Department's hard work and vigilance in identifying the Cali cartel's front companies and agents is helping cut the economic lifeline of one of the most notorious drug rings in the world," McCurry said.
